artifacts.description: Scene analysis — closing scene.
artifacts.notes: Split from scene-analysis 3.4.0. Position is no longer a conditional inside one template: a first scene has no narrative context, a continuing scene has all prior scenes, a closing scene has the whole story — and each pairs with an output contract whose continuity fields match. The instruction body is shared (instructionBlockKey). 2.0.0 is the Stage 2 last-scene analysis of 2026-10-10, brought up to date with the first and nth scenes: the plain style, the bounded Stage 1 block, every earlier scene's record (PRIOR_SCENES) in place of the character roster, the location registry and the accumulated narrative, and the themes already used. It asks what this scene shows about the threads the earlier records carry, as a closure list sent to the closing scene alone (output template scene-last 2.0.0, schema 3.3.0); the closing scene may mark climax or resolution, never inciting or midpoint.

artifacts.description: Scene entity extraction (NER) system prompt — extraction-only role, distinct from the scene analyst.
Scene-level named-entity extraction (NER) — non-speaking characters and objects, matched against the parser's own known-entity gazetteer.
artifacts.notes: Wired into the first-pass pipeline: SceneAnalyzer.Analyze calls this prompt before scene-analysis-first/nth/last, and non_speaking_characters/objects were removed from scene-schema.json (3.0.0) in the same change — this is now the sole source non_speaking_characters.go and observed_objects.go read from. Deliberately narrower than scene-analysis: no accumulated prior-scene context, no narrative reasoning, no significance judgment. It reads the scene text in front of it and reports, for every entity the text names, whether it matches one of the known entities supplied (this scene's own speaking characters, plus every location in the screenplay, from the parser) or is new, plus every physical object the text names. Surface forms are recorded as observed, never normalised, canonicalised, or merged — relating differently-described mentions of the same thing is a later pass. 1.1.0 (#771) splits KNOWN_ENTITIES into a labelled cast and a labelled location list: 1.0.0 supplied both as one flat bullet list, so a location was indistinguishable from a character, and on a screenplay with no dialogue the whole block was a single unlabelled bullet naming a place. The model reported those places as people — 65 of 97 warnings on a 62-scene fixture. Locations are now the whole screenplay's rather than this scene's alone, because they serve as an exclusion set and a scene's action can name a place whose slugline belongs elsewhere.

artifacts.description: Scene-level relation extraction — relations the scene text states between entities on a supplied known-entity roster, as observed surface forms.
artifacts.notes: Second per-scene extraction pass (Stage 2 NER), run after entity minting completes so the roster carries minted observed characters and objects. KNOWN_ENTITIES here is the package-read relation roster (relationRoster), never buildKnownEntities — the entity pass's gazetteer deliberately skips non-speaking characters, which are exactly the entities this pass exists to relate. The prompt instructs the model to name endpoints exactly as the roster lists them; endpoint resolution is a Go-side exact lookup in the roster's own name-key map, a miss is a reported finding and no deposit. Relations are surface forms only: label as stated, grounding line quoted, no taxonomy — record as observed, relating differently-described mentions is not this pass's job either.
